4390.stem:
The table shows monthly repayments for each \$1000 borrowed.

\exfigure{300_q29_1}

figures.cap: monthly repayment table per $1000 borrowed (picture of table)

parts.latex:
A couple borrows \$520 000 to buy a house at $8\%$ per annum over 25 years.

How much does the couple repay in total for this loan?

Chris borrows some money at $7\%$ per annum. Chris will repay the loan over 15 years, paying \$3596 per month.

How much money does Chris borrow?

solutions.latex:
The table gives the repayment per \$1000 borrowed, $\$7.72$ for $8\%$ over 25 years.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Monthly repayment} &= \dfrac{520\,000}{1000}\times 7.72\\ &= \$4014.40\end{aligned}$$
There are $12\times 25$ monthly repayments.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Total repaid} &= 4014.40\times 12\times 25\\ &= \$1\,204\,320\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Calculates the monthly repayment, or equivalent merit
Identifies the correct factor from the table, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The table factor for $7\%$ over 15 years is $8.99$ per \$1000.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Amount borrowed} &= \dfrac{3596}{8.99}\times 1000\\ &= \$400\,000\end{aligned}$$

300_q29_1.notes: This is a typeset table, so I transcribed it instead of drawing it (rule 8, rule 15 spans). The frame line 'Principal and Interest per $1000 borrowed' is kept as the caption subtitle. 'Interest rate (per annum)' spans both header rows. 'Term of loan (years)' spans all six term columns.

parts.latex: What are the values of $A$ and $B$?

After 50 months of repaying the loan, Frankie decides to make a lump sum payment of \$40 000 and to continue making the monthly repayments of \$1485. The loan will then be fully repaid after a further 146 monthly repayments.

How much less will Frankie pay overall by making the lump sum payment?

solutions.latex:
Monthly rate is $\dfrac{7.2\%}{12} = 0.6\% = 0.006$.

Interest is charged on the previous balance.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= 199\,715 \times 0.006 \\ &= \$1198.29 \end{aligned}$$
The new balance is the previous balance plus interest less the repayment.
$$\begin{aligned} B &= 199\,428.29 + 1196.57 - 1485 \\ &= \$199\,139.86 \end{aligned}$$

Total number of repayments:
$$50 + 146 = 196$$
Total paid with the lump sum:
$$\begin{aligned} 196\times 1485 + 40\,000 &= \$331\,060 \end{aligned}$$
Total paid under the original arrangement:
$$\begin{aligned} 23\times 12\times 1485 &= \$409\,860 \end{aligned}$$
The saving is
$$\begin{aligned} 409\,860 - 331\,060 &= \$78\,800 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Calculates the total repayments under the original arrangements OR finds the total number of repayments made

4518.stem:
Select the sheet named ‘Monthly Payments’ from the options at the bottom of the spreadsheet to answer parts a), b) and c).

Kim plans to borrow $\$400\,000$ over 30 years at the rate of $5.8\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.

parts.latex: How much is the balance owing on the loan after 50 months.
After how many months is half of the loan paid off?

Each monthly payment is used to pay off a portion of the money borrowed and the interest owed on the loan.

Which is the first period number in which more than half the monthly repayment goes towards paying off the principal?
Explain how the interest paid on a loan is lower if payments are made with fortnightly frequency as compared to if the repayments are monthly.

solutions.latex:
From the ‘Monthly Payments’ spreadsheet, the balance after 50 months is
$$\$376\,666.22$$

From the spreadsheet, half of the loan is paid off after
$$250 \text{ months}$$

From the spreadsheet, the first period in which more than half of the repayment goes towards the principal is
$$\text{period } 218$$

With the extra payment, the spreadsheet shows the loan is paid off in 341 months instead of 360 months.
$$360 - 341 = 19 \text{ months}$$
Hence the loan term decreases by 19 months.

Compare the total interest paid under monthly and fortnightly repayments.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Difference} &= 444\,925.72 - 352\,404.22 \\ &= \$92\,521.50 \end{aligned}$$
Yes, Suzy's claim is true, as Kim saves $\$92\,521.50$ in interest by switching the payment frequency.
More frequent repayments reduce the balance brought forward, which lowers the interest added each period. A higher portion of each repayment then pays off the balance.
criteria: Explains that the balance brought forward is reduced, lowering the interest added each period, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Navneet and her husband want to buy a house. Their combined gross income is $\$9836.67$ per month. They can afford $25\%$ of their gross monthly income for loan repayments. The couple are already paying off a car loan at $\$260$ per month.

The bank offers a loan with monthly repayments of $\$8.36$ per $\$1000$ borrowed.

Calculate the largest loan that this couple can afford, to the nearest thousand.

solutions.latex:
Find $25\%$ of the gross monthly income.
$$25\%\times 9836.67 = \$2459.17$$
Subtract the car loan repayment.
$$2459.17 - 260 = \$2199.17$$
The repayment is $\$8.36$ per $\$1000$, so divide to find the number of thousands.
$$2199.17\div 8.36 \approx 263.0586$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Maximum loan} = 263.0586\times 1000 \approx \$263\,000$$
criteria: Finds the available repayment after the car loan ($\$2199.17$), or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Michael takes a loan of $\$450\,000$ over a period of 25 years at a reducible interest rate of $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly.

Repayments $R$ are made monthly.

Using the table of present value interest factors below and the recurrence relation,

$$A_{n+1} = A_n(1+r) - R$$

Calculate how much interest has been charged on the loan after the second repayment.

\extable{3314_q8_t1}

solutions.latex:
The monthly rate and number of repayments are
$$r = 6\%\div 12 = 0.5\% ,\qquad n = 25\times 12 = 300$$
From the table, the interest factor is $155.2069$, so
$$\begin{aligned} R &= 450\,000\div 155.2069 \\ &= \$2899.36 \end{aligned}$$
Using $A_{n+1} = A_n(1+r) - R$ with $A_0 = 450\,000$:
$$\begin{aligned} A_1 &= 450\,000(1.005) - 2899.36 = \$449\,350.64 \\ A_2 &= 449\,350.64(1.005) - 2899.36 = \$448\,698.03 \end{aligned}$$
The loan has reduced by
$$450\,000 - 448\,698.03 = \$1301.97$$
The total repayments are
$$2\times 2899.36 = \$5798.72$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Interest} &= 5798.72 - 1301.97 \\ &= \$4496.75 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the loan reduction, or equivalent merit

4596.stem:
Matt borrowed \$35 000. Interest is charged at the end of every month. He then makes a repayment of \$2140. The table below sets out his monthly repayment schedule for the first 4 months of the loan. The loan will be repaid after 17 months.

\extable{15_q31_t1}

parts.latex: Show that the monthly interest rate is 0.275%.

At the end of the first year, when \$10 100.64 was still owing, Matt decided to pay the loan off in full. He was charged a \$50 fee for paying off his loan early. How much less will Matt pay overall by paying his loan off early?

meta.format_note: Source gives $90.63 and $90.62 as the two methods (rounding difference); kept as is.

solutions.latex:
There are $5$ months of repayments remaining if he continues, each of $\$2140$.
$$2140 \times 5 = \$10\,700$$
If he pays off early, he pays the amount owing plus the fee.
$$10\,100.64 + 50 = \$10\,150.64$$
The final repayment is not a full $\$2140$: it is only $\$1621.28$ (see the spreadsheet), so the remaining payments total
$$4\times 2140 + 1621.28 = \$10\,181.28$$
The saving is
$$10\,181.28 - 10\,150.64 = \$30.64$$
Alternatively, adding the next 5 months of interest:
$$(27.78 + 21.97 + 16.14 + 10.30 + 4.45) - 50 = \$30.64$$
$$\therefore\ \text{He saves } \$30.64$$
(The schools guideline gave $10\,700 - 10\,150.64 = \$549.36$, assuming five full repayments.)
criteria: Finds the total of the remaining repayments ($\$10\,181.28$), or equivalent merit

meta.marker_note: Alternative method: $-1$ for the error shown.
meta.correction_note: Claude 23 Nov (Standard batch 1 verify): the schools answer $549.36 assumed five full $2140 repayments; the loan ends with $1621.28, so the saving is $30.64

4341.stem:
William has a reducing balance loan on which he owes \$5590. He makes monthly repayments of \$110.

The loan company charges interest at $24\%$ per annum, compounded monthly.

The spreadsheet shows some of the information for the next two months of the loan.

parts.latex:
Complete the entries in the spreadsheet to show the balance owing on the loan at the end of two months.

\extable{40_q21_t1}
Explain why the loan will never be repaid if William continues to make repayments of \$110 per month.

solutions.latex:
The monthly interest rate is $\dfrac{24\%}{12} = 2\%$.

Month 1:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Interest} &= 0.02 \times 5590 = \$111.80 \\ \text{Balance} &= 5590 + 111.80 - 110 = \$5591.80 \end{aligned}$$
Month 2:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Interest} &= 0.02 \times 5591.80 = \$111.84 \\ \text{Balance} &= 5591.80 + 111.84 - 110 = \$5593.64 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Balance at the end of two months} = \$5593.64$$
criteria: Finds the balance after one month, \$5591.80, or equivalent merit

meta.generated_note: Spreadsheet layout not visible; entries given as interest and closing balance for each month.

solutions.latex:
The interest charged each month is about \$111.80, which is more than the repayment of \$110.

So the balance increases each month and the loan will never be repaid.

parts.latex:
A couple borrows \$30 000 to be repaid in equal monthly repayments of \$280 over 10 years.

After following this repayment plan for 5 years, they decide to decrease their monthly repayment to \$250. As a result, it will take them an additional two years to pay off their loan.

How much more will they repay in total by making this change?

solutions.latex:
Original plan: $\$280$ per month for $10 \times 12 = 120$ months.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= 280 \times 120 \\ &= \$33\,600 \end{aligned}$$
New plan: $\$280$ for the first 5 years ($60$ months), then $\$250$ for $5+2 = 7$ years ($84$ months).
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= 280 \times 60 + 250 \times 84 \\ &= 16\,800 + 21\,000 \\ &= \$37\,800 \end{aligned}$$
The extra amount repaid is
$$\begin{aligned} 37\,800 - 33\,600 &= \$4200 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{they will repay } \$4200 \text{ more.}$$
criteria: Calculates the total repaid under both plans, or equivalent merit
Calculates the total repaid under one plan, or equivalent merit

meta.self_check: Arithmetic checked; no interest rate needed since the totals are counts of repayments.
meta.generated_note: Worked solution written from the question. Interpreted 'additional two years' as 2 years beyond the original 10, so 7 years at \$250 after year 5.
